prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Choose Your Companion Personality", "Select Companion Trait"]
1: ["How to Interact with Your Desktop Companion", "Control your pet directly from your desktop screen using hotkeys and menu shortcuts."]
2: ["Custom Companion Reference Photo", "Ensure bright lighting and clear framing for optimal desktop pet rendering."]
3: ["Select Your Desktop Companion Journey", "Explore Path Option"]
4: ["Preparing Your Companion Desktop Assets", "Companion Hatching Playground", "Tap to interact with your pet while desktop initialization completes."]
5: ["Signing in saves your pet cloud progress so pets are not reset when opening the desktop app later."]
6: ["Your Desktop Pet is Ready!", "Your new companion is initialized and ready to roam your screen.", "Launch Desktop Pet"]
7: ["Name Your Desktop Companion", "Choose a unique name for your pet before final customization."]
8: ["Includes Starter Companion Pack"]
9: ["Sign In to Protect Your Desktop Pet", "Connect your account to enable cloud saving and guard against companion data loss."]

verdicts.problem: Asks for personal information by requesting a user reference photo.
Mentions included free extras or promotional companion packs.
